title: Burghley to Walsingham, Westminster 5 July 1572: name codes in a letter-book copy, BL Harley MS 260 f. 262 (DECODE R8358)

documents.shelfmark: BL Harley MS 260 ff. 262r-262v; DECODE R8358

plaintext.source: Letter printed in Digges, The Compleat Ambassador (1655), July 1572, with the cipher left as figures; Walsingham's 13 July reply there too. No decipherment found.

transcription.notes: Boxed codes [2] [3] [4] [5], monogram ⅌B, single letters A and F, one five-letter run m o R d A.

system.summary: Small name code of boxed digits, single letters and a monogram, plus one short letter run; inserted in a clear letter.
system.notes: Copy in a letter-book; the codes were copied from the sent letters.

prior_solution.where: Digges 1655 prints the letter and the reply with the cipher unread; CSP Foreign x July 1572 does not calendar them

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Downloaded the two R8358 images with the DECODE cookie.
Identified the pages as Walsingham's letter-book: Burghley to Walsingham, Westminster 5 July 1572 (DECODE pages in reverse order).
Found the letter and Walsingham's 13 July reply in Digges 1655, cipher printed as figures.
Searched CSP Foreign x July 1572 (BHO pp. 140-163) for the letter or a decipherment.
Checked sibling records R8356-R8364 and Tomokiyo's Elizabethan survey for a 1572 Walsingham key.
Code [3] = the French King from context and Walsingham's reply.
Applied r8361's rule (box after a word marks a cover-name) to 'Milan [4]'; [2], [5], monogram, A, F and the run m o R d A get no value.

outcome.notes: Explained and in print; one code identified by context; the rest needs the key.

gaps.item: letter run m o R d A
